answer: One defense is to require each agent to post a refundable bond before it can influence a market or vote. The protocol caps an agent’s influence by its bonded stake, then slashes the bond if the agent breaks a verifiable rule, such as signing conflicting orders. Splitting one identity into a hundred does not multiply voting weight unless the attacker locks up a hundred bonds; the cost is capital tied up, plus losses if caught. A juniper market might price a relic in cedar tokens, but the bond rule works across all three.
